ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Acid-dependent drug absorption

A patient takes an oral medicine whose absorption depends on an acidic gastric environment. After famotidine is added, plasma exposure to that medicine falls despite unchanged dosing and adherence. Which change produced by famotidine most directly explains this interaction?

  1. Famotidine universally induces CYP3A4
  2. The companion drug is converted into histamine
  3. H2 antagonism increases renal filtration of all medicines
  4. Raised gastric pH reduces dissolution or absorption of the companion drug
  5. Famotidine chelates every drug through aluminum
Answer and explanation

Raised gastric pH reduces dissolution or absorption of the companion drug

Acid suppression can reduce absorption of selected pH-dependent medicines; the specific combination requires review.

Option explanations

Raised gastric pH reduces dissolution or absorption of the companion drug: Acid suppression can reduce absorption of selected pH-dependent medicines; the specific combination requires review.

Famotidine chelates every drug through aluminum: Famotidine is not an aluminum-containing binding agent.

Famotidine universally induces CYP3A4: Universal enzyme induction is not its mechanism.

The companion drug is converted into histamine: No conversion to histamine occurs.

H2 antagonism increases renal filtration of all medicines: H2 blockade does not universally increase renal drug clearance.
